display_name: Ofek Hadash — the collective agreements that set Israeli teachers' pay
citation: Collective agreement of 25 December 2008 between the State of Israel and the Teachers' Union of Israel implementing the Ofek Hadash reform, as amended — in particular by the wage agreement of 19 October 2022, the follow-up committee decision of 14 January 2025, and the approved collective agreement of 29 June 2026 made under Chapter 9 of the Law for the Achievement of Budget Objectives and Implementation of Economic Policy for the 2025 Budget Year (Legislative Amendments) 5785-2025
authority: The State of Israel (the Wage Commissioner at the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Education) and the Teachers' Union of Israel (Histadrut HaMorim), as parties to a collective agreement; and, for the 2025-2026 wage reduction, the Knesset

source.note: NOT AN OFFICIAL SOURCE, and the distinction matters here more than it does for a statute row. This subject was read entirely from a third-party published corpus of 282 documents -- collective agreements, ministry circulars, salary tables, the Teachers' Service Regulations and one Act -- each encoded as Akoma Ntoso 3.0 (OASIS LegalDocML). Nothing was fetched from the Ministry of Education or from Reshumot. Digests in the encoding's registers/source-bundle.json are over that corpus's published HTML, at the commit recorded there, which is what the encoding actually read; the corpus records the ministry PDFs behind each page separately in its own provenance blocks. The corpus states its own caveats and the encoding adopts them: the /akn/il/... identifiers are a repository convention and are NOT citable outside that corpus, a single-reader transcription is marked as such and is not a verified one, and missing scan pages are recorded in place rather than closed. See the encoding's SOURCE-LICENSE.md, which carries TWO open questions rather than the usual one.

not_law_note: OFEK HADASH IS NOT LEGISLATION, and a reader who takes it for a statute will misread the whole subject. It is a collective agreement between the State and a trade union, layered with later collective agreements, decisions of a joint bipartite follow-up committee (vaadat maakav) which the agreements make binding, and circulars of the Ministry of Education and the Wage Commissioner. The one Act in the picture -- the 2025 budget law -- works by REFERRING BACK to an approved collective agreement rather than by setting a rate itself, so even the statutory layer routes through the agreements. The subject is filed under il/ because the State of Israel is one of the two parties and the Knesset is the authority for the fiscal chapter; the leaf slug carries 2008, the year of the founding agreement, on the same convention statutes use for their enactment year.
